title: Tuberculosis treatment pathways - first-line, drug-resistant, and alternative regimens

primarySource.label: National Guidelines for Management of Drug-Resistant TB (NTEP, Nov 2024)

policyNote: India-facing: NTEP is highest precedence; WHO is comparative/reference. Paraphrased from cited sources; verify weight-band dosing against the current NTEP release before prescribing. DST context is required before any drug-resistant regimen - never select a DR-TB regimen because 'TB' alone was chosen.

states.label: DST pending
states.note: Molecular/culture result awaited. Do NOT recommend a definitive DR-TB regimen; manage per NTEP diagnostic algorithm while awaiting Xpert/DST.

states.label: Drug-susceptible
states.note: No rifampicin resistance detected → first-line HRZE pathway.

states.label: Rifampicin-resistant (RR-TB)
states.note: RIF resistance is the marker for RR/MDR-TB → DR-TB pathway; classify FQ status next.

states.label: MDR-TB (H+R resistant)
states.note: Resistant to at least isoniazid + rifampicin → DR-TB pathway.

states.label: XDR-TB
states.note: MDR + FQ resistance + resistance to a Group A drug (bedaquiline or linezolid) → 20-month longer oral regimen with specialist input.

states.label: Indeterminate / incomplete DST
states.note: Repeat testing; manage per algorithm; do not default to a DR-TB regimen.

safetyGates.label: Baseline ECG / QTcF
safetyGates.rule: QTcF ≤450 ms (male) / ≤470 ms (female); correct hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia/hypocalcaemia before any QT-prolonging drug; recheck if abnormal.
safetyGates.missingMessage: Baseline ECG / QTcF required - verify before selecting regimen.

safetyGates.label: CBC + peripheral-neuropathy screen (linezolid)
safetyGates.rule: Hb ≥8 g/dL, platelets ≥75,000/mm³, ANC ≥750/mm³; grade 3/4 neuropathy is a relative contraindication; add pyridoxine; monitor CBC (baseline, wk2/4/8) and neuropathy.
safetyGates.missingMessage: CBC and neuropathy screen required for linezolid-containing regimens - verify before selecting.

safetyGates.label: Liver function
safetyGates.rule: Significant liver dysfunction (AST/ALT >3×ULN or total bilirubin >2×ULN) excludes BPaLM; hepatotoxic first-line drugs need LFT monitoring.
safetyGates.missingMessage: Liver function required - verify before selecting regimen.

safetyGates.label: Renal function
safetyGates.rule: Serum creatinine >3×ULN is a relative contraindication to BPaLM; injectables (amikacin/streptomycin) and several drugs need renal dose review.
safetyGates.missingMessage: Renal function required - verify before selecting regimen.

safetyGates.label: Pregnancy / contraception
safetyGates.rule: BPaLM: pregnancy restrictions apply (per current MTP notification). The Lzd-containing 9-11-mo shorter oral regimen may be used in pregnancy with monitoring. Counsel on family planning; rifampicin reduces hormonal-contraceptive efficacy.
safetyGates.missingMessage: Pregnancy status required - verify before selecting regimen.

safetyGates.label: Cardiac / drug-interaction review
safetyGates.rule: Exclude significant cardiac conduction disease, uncontrolled arrhythmia, Torsade risk. Review CYP450 inducers/inhibitors, other QT-prolonging drugs, serotonergic/MAOI, myelosuppressive drugs; separate Mg-containing products from fluoroquinolone by 2h.
safetyGates.missingMessage: Cardiac and interaction review required - verify before selecting regimen.

regimens.name: Standard drug-susceptible TB (HRZE)
regimens.eligibility: Microbiologically-confirmed (or programmatically-diagnosed) drug-susceptible TB; no rifampicin resistance.
regimens.notForUse: Rifampicin resistance detected; documented first-line drug intolerance (use DILI/intolerance pathway).
regimens.duration: 2 months intensive (HRZE) + 4 months continuation (HR); total 6 months (extend for CNS/skeletal/disseminated disease).
regimens.doseRef: Weight-band dosing per NTEP (FDC by weight band).
regimens.dstRequirements: Universal DST for rifampicin (Xpert) at diagnosis; escalate if RIF resistance found.
regimens.escalation: RIF resistance, treatment failure, or hepatotoxicity → reassess; move to DR-TB or DILI pathway.

regimens.name: BPaLM (bedaquiline + pretomanid + linezolid + moxifloxacin)
regimens.eligibility: First choice in eligible persons ≥14 years with MDR/RR-TB, regardless of fluoroquinolone-resistance or HIV status. New microbiologically-confirmed MDR/RR-TB (or probable MDR-TB failing H mono/poly). Bdq/Lzd/Pa exposure <1 month, OR >1 month with documented susceptibility. Baseline QTcF ≤450 ms (M)/≤470 ms (F).
regimens.notForUse: Age <14 years; documented resistance to bedaquiline, linezolid or pretomanid; significant liver dysfunction (AST/ALT >3×ULN or total bilirubin >2×ULN); severe extrapulmonary MDR-TB (CNS, spinal/skeletal, disseminated/miliary); significant cardiac conduction abnormality / uncontrolled arrhythmia / Torsade risk / uncorrectable QTcF prolongation.
regimens.relativeContraindications: Hb <8 g/dL, platelets <75,000/mm³, ANC <750/mm³, serum creatinine >3×ULN, grade 3/4 peripheral neuropathy; interacting drugs (CYP450 inducers/inhibitors, QT-prolonging, serotonergic/MAOI, myelosuppressive).
regimens.duration: 26 weeks (extendable to 39 weeks per criteria, e.g. Lzd dose reduction).
regimens.doseRef: Bedaquiline 400 mg OD weeks 1-2, then 200 mg thrice weekly to week 26/39; pretomanid 200 mg OD; linezolid 600 mg OD; moxifloxacin 400 mg OD; pyridoxine 50 mg (16-29 kg) / 100 mg (>30 kg). No weight-band dosing for the four core drugs (≥14 y). Take orally with food; separate magnesium-containing products by 2 h.
regimens.dstRequirements: May start while awaiting baseline Bdq/Lzd/Pa DST (resistance rates low in India). If baseline DST shows resistance to Bdq/Pa/Lzd → declare 'treatment regimen changed' and switch to 18-20-month longer oral regimen. Moxifloxacin continues full course regardless of FQ resistance.
regimens.escalation: Grade 3/4 Lzd toxicity <9 weeks → treatment failed; Bdq/Pa/Lzd resistance on DST → longer oral regimen; ineligible → 9-11-month shorter oral regimen (then longer oral).

regimens.name: 9-11-month shorter oral MDR/RR-TB regimen
regimens.eligibility: Rifampicin resistance detected; fluoroquinolone resistance NOT detected; no >1-month exposure to second-line drugs in the regimen (Bdq/Lfx/Cfz/Lzd) unless susceptibility confirmed; no extensive disease; no severe extrapulmonary MDR-TB. Preferred over the 18-20-month longer regimen. In ≥14 y, BPaLM is first preference. The Lzd-containing version may be used in pregnancy with monitoring.
regimens.notForUse: Fluoroquinolone resistance; severe extrapulmonary TB (CNS/spinal/skeletal/miliary/disseminated); extensive disease; additional resistance to Z (switch to longer oral).
regimens.duration: 9-11 months. Structure (Lzd version): (2) Lzd + (4-6) Lfx-Cfz-Z-E-Hh + (6-9) Bdq intensive → (5) Lfx-Cfz-Z-E continuation. IP extendable to max 6 months if smear-positive at month 4.
regimens.doseRef: Adult weight-band (16-29 / 30-45 / 46-70 / >70 kg): high-dose H 300/600/900/900 mg; E 400/800/1200/1600 mg; Z 750/1250/1750/2000 mg; Lfx 250/750/1000/1000 mg; Bdq 400 mg daily wk0-2 then 200 mg 3×/wk wk3-24; Cfz 50/100/100/200 mg; Eto 375/500/750/1000 mg; pyridoxine 50/100/100/100 mg. Linezolid 600 mg (≥14 y). Paediatric Lzd by weight band (Table 3.5).
regimens.dstRequirements: Rapid DST to rule out FQ resistance required BEFORE starting. Repeat NAAT/LPA + culture DST if smear-positive at end of IP or culture-positive at month 3+.
baselineIx: ophthalmic (visual acuity + colour vision) at baseline, wk9/13/26
monitoring: CBC for early Lzd toxicity (>10% drop in Hb/neutrophils/platelets)
no TSH needed if Eto not used
regimens.escalation: Z resistance at baseline, or FQ/InhA+KatG on month-4 sample, or ≥2 core drugs stopped → declare treatment failed → switch to 18-20-month longer oral regimen after N/DDR-TBC reassessment.

regimens.name: 18-20-month longer oral M/XDR-TB regimen
regimens.eligibility: Persons ineligible for BPaLM or the 9-11-month shorter regimen (ineligibility, additional resistance, intolerance, drug non-availability), or pre-XDR/XDR-TB. Individualised per DST from Groups A/B/C. Specialist / N-DDR-TBC decision.
regimens.notForUse: Where a shorter all-oral regimen is eligible (prefer shorter).
regimens.duration: 18-20 months (bedaquiline limited to 6 months, extension only if an effective regimen cannot otherwise be built). XDR-TB: 20 months. Backbone: (6+) Bdq + (18-20) Lfx-Lzd-Cfz-Cs.
regimens.doseRef: Adult weight-band Table 3.7: Lfx 250/750/1000/1000; Mfx 200/400/400/400 (high-dose Mfx 400/600/800/800); Bdq as above; Cfz 50/100/100/200; Cs 250/500/750/1000; Lzd 300-600; Dlm 100 mg BD (≥12 y); Am 500/750/750/1000 (≤10 mg/kg, max 750 mg if >60 y); Z 750/1250/1750/2000; Eto 375/500/750/1000; Na-PAS 10/14/16/22 g; E 400/800/1200/1600; imipenem-cilastatin 1 g+1 g BD or meropenem 1 g TID / 2 g BD, each WITH clavulanate (amox-clav 875/125 BD, only with carbapenem); pyridoxine 50/100/100/100.
regimens.dstRequirements: Full DST-driven drug selection (FQ, SLI, Eto, Bdq/Lzd/Pa/Dlm where available). Repeat NAAT/LPA + LC-DST if culture-positive at month 6+.
interactions: multiple QT-prolonging agents (Bdq/Mfx/Cfz/Dlm) - cumulative QT risk
regimens.escalation: Cycloserine psychiatric symptoms, injectable ototoxicity, or non-response → specialist DR-TB centre (DT3C) review.

regimens.name: Isoniazid mono/poly-resistant TB regimen (6 Lfx-R-E-Z)
regimens.eligibility: Isoniazid mono/poly-resistance with rifampicin SUSCEPTIBLE. Regimen (6) Lfx-R-E-Z; no separate IP/CP.
regimens.duration: 6 months; extend directly to 9 months for extensive disease, uncontrolled comorbidity, extrapulmonary TB, month-4 smear-positive, or when the regimen is modified.
regimens.doseRef: Adult weight-band Table 3.8: R 300/450/600/750 mg; E 400/800/1200/1600 mg; Z 750/1250/1750/2000 mg; Lfx 250/750/1000/1000 mg. Replacement (Table 3.9): if Lfx or Z can't be used → Lzd (then Cfz+Cs); if both → 2 of Lzd/Cfz/Cs.
regimens.dstRequirements: Confirm rifampicin susceptibility; FQ susceptibility informs Lfx use.
regimens.escalation: Non-response/failure without additional R resistance → 'probable MDR' → BPaLM/shorter/longer per eligibility.

regimens.name: Individualized DR-TB regimen
regimens.eligibility: Use when standardized regimen eligibility is not met (additional resistance, intolerance, drug non-availability). Built from Groups A/B/C by DST.
regimens.notForUse: When a standardized (BPaLM/shorter/longer) regimen is eligible.
coreMeds: per DST from WHO/NTEP Groups A/B/C
regimens.doseRef: Per Table 3.7 weight bands for the selected drugs.
baselineIx: full DR-TB baseline panel (ECG, CBC, LFT, renal, electrolytes, audiometry/ophthalmic as indicated)
interactions: per constituent drugs (cumulative QT, myelosuppression, oto/nephrotoxicity)

regimens.name: CNS / TB meningitis pathway
regimens.eligibility: TB meningitis / CNS TB. Drug-susceptible: extended-duration HRZE-based therapy with adjunctive corticosteroids; drug-resistant CNS-TB excludes BPaLM (severe EP-TB) → individualized longer regimen with CNS-penetrating drugs.
regimens.notForUse: BPaLM is NOT used for CNS/severe EP-TB.
regimens.duration: Extended total duration (longer continuation phase) per source; corticosteroid taper.
regimens.doseRef: Weight-band first-line dosing; verify CNS-specific duration against source.
regimens.dstRequirements: DST; if RR/MDR → individualized regimen with CNS-penetrating agents (specialist).

regimens.name: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) on anti-TB therapy
regimens.eligibility: Hepatotoxicity during ATT (rising transaminases/bilirubin, symptoms). Stop hepatotoxic drugs, support, reintroduce sequentially once LFTs recover per protocol.
regimens.notForUse: Continuing unchanged hepatotoxic therapy through significant DILI.
coreMeds: non-hepatotoxic holding regimen while LFTs recover (per protocol)
regimens.dstRequirements: N/A for DILI decision; maintain DST context for the underlying TB.
baselineIx: viral hepatitis markers (HBsAg, Hep A/C/E) if jaundiced
regimens.escalation: Severe/fulminant DILI → hepatology/specialist; do NOT generically continue therapy.

regimens.name: TB with renal impairment / dialysis
regimens.eligibility: Renal impairment or dialysis. Renally-cleared anti-TB drugs (E, Z, and injectables, some second-line) need interval/dose adjustment; R and H largely unchanged.
regimens.notForUse: Unadjusted dosing of renally-cleared drugs in significant impairment.
regimens.doseRef: Adjust E/Z (and injectables/second-line) by CrCl; give post-dialysis where applicable; verify against NTEP §3.9.5.

outOfScope.topic: Latent TB infection (LTBI) / TB preventive treatment
outOfScope.note: Not covered by this treatment-pathway module unless already within product scope; marked out of scope.

specialSituations.label: Pregnancy & lactation
specialSituations.guidance: Joint obstetrician + physician management at a DR-TBC. BPaLM only if <20/<24 wk gestation AND willing for MTP (pretomanid not in lactation unless formula-feeding) - so BPaLM generally does NOT apply to pregnant/breastfeeding women. The Lzd-containing 9-11-mo shorter oral regimen is available to all pregnant women (after other eligibility); Eto-based only after 32 wk if Lzd unusable; else 18-20-mo longer oral. Counsel on contraception (OCP efficacy reduced by vomiting + DR-TB drug interactions).
specialSituations.monitoring: Monthly CBC/Hb; USG anomaly scan 18 wk + growth scan 32 wk; more frequent ECG/electrolytes as indicated; TSH monthly if Eto and basal TSH deranged; newborn CBC + TSH if exposed to Lzd/Eto/PAS; deliver where a paediatrician is available.

specialSituations.label: Children (<14 y)
specialSituations.guidance: BPaLM (contains pretomanid) not established <14 y → use 9-11-mo shorter or longer oral regimen per eligibility with a paediatrician. Bedaquiline approved ≥5 y (child-friendly 20 mg dispersible tablet); below 5 y only where regulator-approved (otherwise replace per PMDT). Delamanid 25 mg DT approved from ≥10 kg.
specialSituations.monitoring: Weight-band paediatric dosing (Lzd Table 3.5); paediatric monitoring per regimen.

specialSituations.label: Older people (≥65 y)
specialSituations.guidance: Insufficient trial data for BPaLM (Pa/Bdq/Lzd) in ≥65 y. Assess health status + comorbidities carefully before BPaLM; if used, monitor much more closely. Reduce aminoglycoside dose (≤10 mg/kg, max 750 mg).

specialSituations.label: People living with HIV
specialSituations.guidance: BPaLM can be given regardless of HIV status/CD4 (care if CD4 <100); manage with the ART centre. Interactions: efavirenz induces bedaquiline AND reduces pretomanid - AVOID with BPaLM (prefer dolutegravir); ritonavir raises bedaquiline (monitor QT); avoid zidovudine with linezolid (additive neuropathy + myelosuppression).
specialSituations.monitoring: Joint ART-centre + DR-TBC follow-up; QT and CBC monitoring given interactions.

specialSituations.label: Renal insufficiency / dialysis
specialSituations.guidance: Bedaquiline, linezolid and moxifloxacin are generally safe in renal insufficiency. Renally-cleared drugs (E, Z, cycloserine, aminoglycosides) need interval/dose adjustment; give post-dialysis where applicable. Renal impairment may itself be TB- or prior-aminoglycoside-related.
specialSituations.monitoring: Renal function; drug levels for aminoglycoside.

specialSituations.label: Liver disease / DILI
specialSituations.guidance: Second-line drugs are relatively less hepatotoxic than first-line. On BPaLM, routine LFT at month 3 + as clinically indicated; deranged baseline LFT → strict monitoring. If hepatitis develops, exclude other causes (viral/alcohol/other drugs); stop drugs if significant inflammation. Significant dysfunction (AST/ALT >3×ULN or bilirubin >2×ULN) excludes BPaLM.
specialSituations.monitoring: Serial LFTs; viral markers if jaundiced.

specialSituations.label: Diabetes mellitus
specialSituations.guidance: Glycaemic control is harder in MDR-TB + DM (insulin often needed). Increased peripheral-neuropathy risk (exacerbated by linezolid + high-dose isoniazid) - counsel to report early; may switch to Eto-containing shorter regimen or longer regimen without linezolid. High-dose metformin + linezolid raises lactic-acidosis risk.

specialSituations.label: Anaemia / cytopenia
specialSituations.guidance: Hb <8 g/dL, platelets <75,000/mm³ or ANC <750/mm³ are relative contraindications to linezolid-containing regimens. For iron-deficiency anaemia with Hb <8, transfuse/supplement and start once Hb >8 with close CBC monitoring; if Hb falls <8 on treatment and responds to transfusion, Lzd 600 mg may continue with intensive monitoring.
specialSituations.monitoring: CBC baseline + wk2/4/8; watch >10% drop in Hb/neutrophils/platelets.
